historyReviewBoundary: All 115 histories have author source checks. Final independent review covered metadata and numerical checks for all 115 classes, 12 deeper class targets and source-gap samples in seven classes. It did not independently verify every passage of every cited source.

history.name: Sulfamate-substituted monosaccharide anticonvulsants

starting.description: A synthetic sugar-derived intermediate, selected for planned mouse seizure testing because of its structure, showed anticonvulsant activity. The observed effect supplied the starting point for developing it for epilepsy.

inspiration.description: Anticonvulsant effect observed in a mouse electroshock assay of a pre-existing synthetic sugar-derived intermediate. The earlier program sought analogues of fructose-1,6-diphosphate for a metabolic-enzyme objective; this chemical context is distinct from the observed seizure effect.

steps.description: The compound was made as an intermediate in a program seeking metabolic-enzyme inhibitors for a potential antidiabetic treatment, then selected for a targeted anticonvulsant assay on the basis of structure.
Its observed mouse anticonvulsant effect prompted further evaluation and eventual preclinical development; a contemporaneous patent disclosed both the synthetic compound and animal seizure-test data.
The 1987 report identified the active sugar sulfamate as topiramate and described synthesis and anticonvulsant testing of related analogues.
The candidate progressed through clinical development and received FDA approval for epilepsy in late 1996.

design.description: Researchers made the sulfamate derivative of protected fructose, selected it for seizure testing using a structural clue, assembled supporting pharmacology, pursued preclinical development and synthesized and tested related analogues. The accessible 1987 abstract does not establish that any particular later analogue became a marketed medicine.

circumstances.description: Gardocki deliberately selected the compound for mouse anticonvulsant testing. The cited account does not establish whether the positive result itself was unexpected.

limits: The founding history is supported for topiramate, the packet's only cohort member, and should not be extrapolated automatically to other anticonvulsants or sulfamate compounds.

The original program's metabolic-enzyme-inhibition objective and the later seizure-screening observation are separate; an intended antidiabetic use does not establish an observed antidiabetic effect of topiramate.
gaps: The 1987 original journal article was accessible only as an abstract; its full text was not read.
The original authors overlap across the patent, the 1987 report, and retrospective sources, so these are not independent accounts of the founding chronology.

The specific rationale, if any, for selecting this compound beyond the described interest in its structure and sulfamate-related group is not established by the accessible founding account. The similarity to sulfonamide carbonic-anhydrase inhibitors is tied by S2 to testing carbonic-anhydrase inhibition, not explicitly to the initial seizure test.
